messages:
mira: quick flag — after rolling int4 per-channel quant for nimbus7b-lite to canary, we're seeing a small but actionable quality regression on summarization evals + sporadic OOMs under microbatch=8. looping in infra/sre. :eyes:

kai: can you paste the eval delta and the OOM traces? which kernel path did we pick for int4?

mira: eval: rougeL dropped ~2.3 pts vs fp16 baseline on our internal news-summary suite (stable prompt set). perf/canary numbers: p50+p95 stable, p99 +15% on long-context requests. OOM rate ~0.8% on canary traffic (vs 0.0% prev). kernel chosen: "sparse-attn-simd" with hybrid-kv caching. config snippet we used: ```
model: nimbus7b-lite
quant: int4_perchannel
kernel_policy: sparse-attn-simd
batching:
  microbatch: 8
  max_batch_ms: 12
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  prefetch_kv: true
```

ashley-sre: I pulled the kube logs from the failing pod. OOM stack shows allocation spike when handling long batch of multiple sessions. snippet: ```
2024-06-12T14:02:11Z ERROR OOM: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
stack: runtime::alloc_buffer -> kv_cache::ensure_space -> forward_attention
context: seq_len=1536, total_batch_tokens=12288
```

leo-ml: interesting — int4 per-channel reduces model size but increases working set on some optimized kernels because we tile differently. hybrid-kv + microbatch=8 can blow up transient GPU allocations for long sequences.

mira: hypothesis: combination of kernel scheduling + prefetch_kv is inflating peak. Also quality regression might be from aggressive per-channel rounding (we used minmax quant calibration on a small dataset).

kai: suggestions: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 128 for this model on canary; 2) flip prefetch_kv=false to avoid preallocing large KV for each microbatch; 3) try alternate kernel path `dense-fast` (less aggressive tiling) for int4 to compare OOM behavior; 4) run quant calibration with larger calibration set / per-layer MSE-clip.

mira: agreed. I'll push a canary patch with these 3 knobs and re-run the rouge/eval sweep + canary traffic. planning: rollout patch to 10% -> collect 24h metrics -> escalate to 50% if OOM rate <0.1% and rouge delta <0.5.

tess-prod: please update rollback/auto-fallback policy so we revert to int8 for sequences >1024 tokens automatically if OOM observed. Product worried about visible user regressions.

mira: noted. adding automatic fallback rule: if seq_len>1024 && model_variant==int4 -> route to int8-variant. will add to rollout policy.

leo-ml: for the quality side, we'll re-run quantize with per-layer scale clipping and test with 5k calibration samples across domains (news, docs, code). should reduce rouge drop. also add eval comparing top-k logits distance to fp16.

ashley-sre: infra action: pin kernel affinity on canary hosts to avoid churn across processes, and add soft-cgroup mem limit to catch bad allocs before OOMing node. I'll open infra ticket.

mira: also seeing a small diff in sampled outputs — more truncated endings on summaries. that points to tokenizer or max_new_tokens interplay. lowering max_new_tokens first is low-risk.

dev-bot: canary-patch created: PR #4127 by mira -> testing queue.

kai: timeline? if we have metric snapshot in ~4 hours we can decide to rollback or continue.

mira: starting patch deploy now to 10% canary. will post updates here with eval numbers and stack traces if anything pops. thanks all. :thumbsup:
